title: Tommy Dorsey as a bandleader and the vocalists
summary: Leeman stayed six or seven months; he describes Dorsey as beautiful to those he liked, hotheaded but quick to apologize, and says Sinatra joined as he left.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: What were you saying?
That was June 19th that I joined Tommy, and I was with him for about 6 or 7 months, which was a wonderful association - we went to Chicago, but I had had enough.
How did you like Tommy?
He was beautiful.
What kind of a man was he?
If he liked somebody, he was a beautiful man.
But if he didn't like you, what happened?
Well, he could give you a bad time.
Well, why would he hire you if he didn't like you?
If he didn't like you, he would hire you if you were a great musician.
Uh huh.
He would make all sorts of excuses for anybody with talent. But he was a hotheaded Irishman, and he
would turn around in two seconds and say, 'I'm sorry' -- which people never gave him that much credit for. He was always fighting with Frank Sinatra and ...
Frank --
I don't know, I can't even say the words I want to say.
Well, while we're on this thing, you said that Frank Sinatra was with Tommy -- were you with Tommy's band when Frank Sinatra was the vocalist?
No, he joined just as I left.
Oh, I see.
Our vocalist was ...
Just wanted to clarify that. Was who?
We had a female vocalist, Edith Wright, and they left at the same time -- and Jack Leonard.
